Method of Attack: Remote access trojan (RAT) maintaining access to host
Includes seven variants of rootkit supporting multiple Linux kernel versions
Rootkit masquerades as unsigned VMware driver
Rootkit hides/unhides ports, makes processes invisible, provides root privilege, kills processes, hides malware-related files and directories
Communicates with command and control (C2) server using RTSP protocol
Possible deployment via botnet or sold by initial access brokers
Potential delivery after exploiting vulnerabilities, credential brute force, or download from untrusted sources impersonating legitimate products
Impacted Systems: Linux systems of telecommunications companies in Thailand
Attack Vector: Download from untrusted sources as package or binary impersonating legitimate product
Indicators of Compromise: Nine distinct hardcoded C2 IP addresses
